solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Piece of evidence vital, barrister reviewed case

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the hidden run is read backwards
a piece of the run of words evidence vital barrister is taken, letters spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A lawyer looks back over a court case and finds one crucial item of evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal case after barrister, but it is the grammatical one. The run EVITALBA spans the end of evidence, all of vital and the start of barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is one of the noun cases, alongside nominative, accusative and the rest.

clue.text: Host, daft going topless

indicators.note: going topless means the top letter, the first of the word, is lost

parts.note: barmy is British slang for daft or crazy

explanation.surface: A dinner host gets silly and strips off their top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the first letter is the top, so 'going topless' removes the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, especially an armed one, as in the heavenly host, so it is a synonym for a large military force.

clue.text: Don't take the washing in, have some fun!

definitions.meaning: the literal instruction to leave every item pegged up on the line outside
the idiom for being uninhibited and relaxing completely

explanation.surface: Laundry day advice: forget the clothes on the line and go and enjoy yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes leaving all the washing dangling outdoors, and idiomatically means abandoning restraint and enjoying yourself.

clue.text: Having abandoned parking, chap later travelling on the tube?

indicators.note: travelling means the letters move about into a new order
having abandoned says a letter is left behind and taken out of the next word

parts.note: taken as written before the letter is removed
P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who has left his car somewhere rides the London Underground afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' looks like the London Underground; it is the windpipe. Removing P from chap leaves CHA, which with LATER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, a tube in the throat, so the adjective describes what relates to or sits in that tube.

clue.text: Rev's sound study, maybe, in support of vicar at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, something in support of another sits beneath it
at first means only the opening letter of vicar is used

parts.note: a study is one example of a room in a house

explanation.surface: A clergyman's study, perhaps, holds up the vicar; Rev looks like his title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a clergyman beside vicar, but it is an engine revving.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the roar of an engine being revved, so it is the noise a revving motor makes.

clue.text: Briefly observe man in hat

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to clock something is British slang for noticing or observing it
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A quick glimpse of a man wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a close-fitting bell-shaped hat for women, popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: African in old party, rather upstanding

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal Party, a British party now merged into the Liberal Democrats

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the word stands up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: nay is used to mean rather, correcting oneself: good, nay excellent

explanation.surface: An African belonged to a former political party and was a fairly upright member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' looks like praise; in a down clue it turns NAY upwards to YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a native of Libya, a North African country, so the noun names one kind of African.

clue.text: Figures, perhaps, in red book

parts.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, after the robes of cardinals
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Some figures are written in red ink in an accounts book.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers such as one, two and three are written as figures, so the phrase is an example of them.

clue.text: All, for example, hairline fractures?

indicators.note: fractures says EG is broken open with the other piece set in the gap

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
a hairline crack is very thin

explanation.surface: Are all these, for instance, tiny hairline cracks in a bone?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairline fractures' reads as a medical phrase; here 'fractures' is a verb and EG splits around VERY THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means the whole lot, every single thing, so it is a synonym for all.

clue.text: Poet: meddlesome man finally getting up after mid-morning?

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the time of day

parts.note: ten o'clock is a time in the middle of the morning

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the letters rise, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nosy person is meddlesome, prying into others' affairs

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of man is used

explanation.surface: A poet watches a busybody finally rising from bed late in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting up' is the reversal signal for a down clue: the busybody and the last letter of man are read upwards, giving NYSON, set after the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate who wrote The Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: Force contained, one calmer?

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's police force
had means held or contained

explanation.surface: Police kept a disturbance under control, and one officer was the cooler head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb; it is the Met, the London police.
explanation.definitionFit: The drug is a synthetic opioid used to calm withdrawal in heroin addicts, so it is a sedative or calmer of sorts.

clue.text: Bombardment, after withdrawal of artillery, lighter perhaps?

indicators.note: after withdrawal of means the following letters are pulled out of the bombardment word

parts.note: a barrage is a heavy bombardment of artillery fire
RA stands for the Royal Artillery, a British Army regiment

explanation.surface: Once the big guns are pulled back after shelling, things feel lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparative of light; it is a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed boat that ferries cargo to and from ships, a type of barge.

clue.text: Long throw has opener dismissed

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, which is dismissed or removed, with a cricket flavour

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, as with a ball

explanation.surface: A cricket image: a long throw comes in and the opening batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the throw; it is a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an itch for something is to yearn for it, so as verbs both mean to desire strongly.

clue.text: Undertake urban regeneration programme? Fraudulent practice

definitions.meaning: read as three words, the phrase means to repair a town, fixing up a whole city
habitual lying and deception, dishonest behaviour

explanation.surface: A council regeneration scheme turns out to be a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into three words it describes repairing a city; as one word it means untruthfulness, the habit of lying.

clue.text: Country squire originally wearing creamy-white jacket?

parts.note: ivory is the creamy-white colour of elephant tusk

indicators.note: wearing puts the squire's letter inside the garment, as a person is inside clothes

parts.note: a coat is a jacket, an outer garment

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of squire is used

explanation.surface: A country squire sports a cream-coloured jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the squire; it is the definition, a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the former English name of Côte d'Ivoire, a West African nation.

clue.text: Packing case shortly, soldier heading for old South American city

indicators.note: packing says the shortened case holds the soldier inside it
shortly means the word is cut short, its last letter lost

parts.note: a valise is a small travelling case
a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of old is used

explanation.surface: A soldier packs a small case before heading for an old city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: VALISE shortened is VALIS, which packs PARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valparaíso is a major port city on the Pacific coast of Chile.

clue.text: Rise in winners for Greek hero

indicators.note: in places the rise inside the winners

parts.note: aces are winning serves in tennis, so winners
a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A climb up the rankings among champions, fitting for a hero of Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the warrior hero of Homer's Iliad, the greatest Greek fighter at Troy.

clue.text: Party hit

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a lively celebration or do

explanation.surface: A party that was a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is slang for a big celebration; as a verb it means to strike violently.

clue.text: Requirement for the wet blanket

definitions.meaning: something people out in the rain need to keep dry
as an adjective, covering everything, all-embracing

explanation.surface: A wet blanket is a killjoy who needs cheering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet blanket' reads as a killjoy; split, 'the wet' are rained-on people and 'blanket' is the all-covering sense.
explanation.definitionFit: You carry one in the rain, and as an adjective, as in umbrella term, it means covering a broad range, like blanket.

clue.text: Between two rivers, what was that German region?

indicators.note: between places the exclamation inside, with a river on either side

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, so two rivers give a pair of Rs
uh is the exclamation of someone who did not catch what was said

explanation.surface: Someone asks again which German region lies between two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is the industrial heartland of western Germany, named after the river that runs through it.

clue.text: Marvel when one starts to hit problems in retirement, and soldiers on

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, retreating, so the pieces are read in reverse
starts to means the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Someone retires and things go wrong, yet the troops carry on: a remarkable thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' turns ONE plus H and P round to PHENO.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is an extraordinary person or thing, and the word also means a prodigy or wonder.

clue.text: Spirit one's necked

definitions.meaning: courage or nerve, as in losing one's nerve
a thing that has a neck, such as a glass container for drink

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang it means courage, and a glass container with a narrow neck is one too.

clue.text: Container, and bags for pets

definitions.note: here pets is a verb, so it matches a verb ending in s

parts.note: a can is a metal container
bags of something means lots, like oodles

explanation.surface: A tin, plus bags, needed for one's pet animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' looks like animals; it is a verb, cuddles.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to kiss and cuddle them, the same as to canoodle.

clue.text: Music centre: last of records on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting on top of the next piece
last of means the final letter of records is used

parts.note: the core is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A music centre plays a record on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music centre' reads as a stereo system; split, music is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written music of a composition, especially for film or orchestra.

clue.text: Curious leader in parliamentary seat

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious

indicators.note: leader in means the first letter of parliamentary is used

explanation.surface: An odd party leader holds a parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a constituency; it is the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Seat is a polite word for the backside, and a rump is an animal's or person's hindquarters.

clue.text: Boss is a virile chap

definitions.meaning: a knob or raised ... on a surface, such as a shield
a sexually potent man, a ladies' man

explanation.surface: The boss is a real ladies' man.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round knob, the same as an ornamental stud; a stud is also slang for a virile man.

clue.text: Boarding towards rear of ship, look up

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for at or towards the stern
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Getting on at the back of a ship, a passenger glances upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means high above or overhead, especially up in a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Soothing heart of fellow, time one loosened bandages

indicators.note: bandages means the rearranged letters wrap around the middle piece
loosened means the letters of time and one are slackened into a new order
heart of means the middle letters of fellow are used

explanation.surface: A soothing sight: a nurse loosens a fellow's bandages over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loosened' is the anagram signal, making EMOIENT, and 'bandages' means that anagram wraps around the heart of fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a softening, calming substance, and as an adjective it means soothing or mollifying.

clue.text: Hat fitter making an adjustment

indicators.note: making an adjustment means the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hatter adjusts a customer's hat for size.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT FOR TAT is Cockney rhyming slang for hat, shortened to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is old British slang for a hat, from rhyming slang tit for tat.

clue.text: Within plant, circuits failed again

indicators.note: within puts the circuits inside the plant

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass, a plant
laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: Inside a factory, the electrical circuits have broken down once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'circuits' suggest a factory's wiring; they are a reed and laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a former bad state, so it is to fail again after improving.
